notes.3: This question was found difficult by most candidates and was probably the one that was attempted the least successfully. Candidates were required to perform manipulations of logarithms that were unable to be done by calculator and so a good basic knowledge of the laws governing logarithms was necessary. (i ) The key to a successful solution for this part of the question was to obtain 32 in powers of either 2 or 4. Having done this, the link between the given information and the required result would have been more clear. Most candidates found this part of the question very difficult and not many obtained correct solutions. (ii) A basic application of the laws of logs was the starting point for this question. Most of the candidates who attempted this part were able to recognise that log q = 1 and gain credit for this. 2 p 4 p 5 5

notes.9: It was evident that some candidates found the concept of functions, especially that of the notation and vocabulary used, difficult. This is an area of the syllabus that may need to be concentrated upon. (i) Candidates should always be encouraged to look at the mark allocation for a question; it will usually give a fair indication of the amount of work necessary. Use of the correct notation was expected i.e. y or g( x ). (ii) Finding the inverse of a given function is a technique that most candidates can do reasonably well and this question was no exception, with some candidates making the odd algebraic/arithmetic slip. Again, use of correct notation was expected from candidates. (iii) The relationships between domains and ranges of functions and their inverses prove to be a difficult concept for many candidates as this part of the question showed. Very few candidates realised that they could merely make use of their answer to part (i) . Yet again, a correct form of notation was expected from candidates. notes.10: With the new format of the question paper, questions involving the plotting of graphs are always laid out so that there is room for candidates to draw in a table of their own for the new variables that are required. Candidates should be encouraged to make use of the space. (i) Candidates were expected to plot y against sin x and this was done by many. There are still many candidates who do not realise that they need to manipulate the given variables in order to obtain a form that will produce a suitable straight line graph when plotted against each other. As in the past, there were some candidates that just plotted y against x . Those candidates that did this could gain few marks in this question. (ii) Provided a suitable graph had been drawn, most candidates realised that using their gradient enabled them to find the value of A and that the intercept of the line with the y -axis gave them the value for B . (iii) Both substitution methods and use of their graph were acceptable for this part of the question. A large majority of candidates were able to give the correct estimate.
